content: Fostemsavir is indicated for use in combination with other antiretroviral drugs for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults who have multidrug-resistant HIV-1 and are failing their current antiretroviral therapy regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety concerns. The recommended dosage is 600 mg orally twice daily. No dosage adjustment is required for patients with any severity of hepatic or renal impairment, including those undergoing hemodialysis. However, the safety and efficacy of fostemsavir in these populations have not been fully established. Amobarbital decreases the plasma levels and effects of fostemsavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes, which metabolize fostemsavir. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it significantly reduces the active moiety (temsavir) plasma concentrations, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. Apalutamide also decreases fostemsavir levels through CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated for the same reasons as above. Bosentan reduces fostemsavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced efficacy and virologic failure. Butabarbital, butalbital, carbamazepine, dabrafenib, efavirenz, enzalutamide, fosphenytoin, ivosedinib, lorlatinib, lumacaftor/ivacaftor, mitotane, nafcillin, pentobarbital, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, rifampin, rifapentine, and St. John’s Wort all decrease fostemsavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with these drugs is contraindicated, as it significantly reduces temsavir plasma concentrations, leading to potential virologic failure and resistance. Adagrasib and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsade de Pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, more frequent monitoring is recommended. Amisulpride and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Artemether and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Fostemsavir increases the levels of atogepant by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, the recommended dosage of atogepant is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. Belzutifan decreases fostemsavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Fostemsavir is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inducers, and belzutifan, as a moderate CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce the conversion of fostemsavir to its active form. Fostemsavir and betibeglogene autotemcel should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed, as they may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. Buprenorphine (in all forms, including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Clarithromycin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Fostemsavir increases the levels of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative HCV regimens should be used, as higher grazoprevir exposure may increase the risk of ALT elevations. Elivaldogene autotemcel and fostemsavir should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications should be discontinued at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization medications and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Fexinidazole and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Avoid combining fexinidazole with drugs that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. Fostemsavir and lovotibeglogene autotemcel should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting antiretrovirals may require a longer discontinuation period. Fostemsavir increases the levels of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Fostemsavir increases the levels of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting OATP1 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Fostemsavir increases the levels of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 and BCRP transporters. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative HCV regimens should be used, as higher voxilaprevir exposure may increase the risk of ALT elevations. Fostemsavir increases the levels of zavegepant intranasal by inhibiting OATP1B3 transporters. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Albuterol and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Alfuzosin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Fostemsavir increases the levels of alpelisib by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Therapy should be modified, or close monitoring is recommended. If possible, avoid co-administration or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates. Fostemsavir increases the levels of ambrisentan by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Therapy should be modified, or close monitoring is recommended. If possible, avoid co-administration or adjust the dose of OATP1B1/3 substrates. Amiodarone and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Amitriptyline and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Anagrelide and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Apomorphine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Arformoterol and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Aripiprazole and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Arsenic trioxide and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Artemether/lumefantrine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Asenapine (including transdermal formulations) and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Atomoxetine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely.
